Approximate analysis of the messy, two-lobed bulk front of this CME, based on the fit with three coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1). There is clear northward deflection from the source location of the M-class flare (N14W13) but the associated erupting filament seems to originate a bit to the west from the flare location and is then seen deflecting northwardly, so the coronal signatures generally confirm this analysis. The half-width of the CME is based on later imagery in STEREO A COR2, as in coronagraphs there is/are later, wider, lobe(s) of this CME that seem to be integral part of it.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from AR 4455 (centered near N25E35) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and near the northeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-06-01T03:00Z. An opening of field lines is seen over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/193, GOES SUVI 171/195/284, and STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery. Additionally, dimming is seen northeast of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 193 imagery and post eruptive arcades begin to form around 2026-06-01T05:00Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-01T19:00Z. This CME is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. This is the slower and wider of two overlapping CMEs. There are a series of coronal signatures likely associated with these two CMEs. This first is some ejecta seen over the W limb in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-06-01T17:57Z. There are also some post-eruptive arcades best seen in STEREO A EUVI starting around 2026-06-01T18:55Z to the W of a small, SW coronal hole. Another coronal signature is a field line movement seen over the SW in STEREO A EUVI 195, GOES SUVI 284, and SDO AIA 171/193 beginning around 2026-06-01T18:30Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-02T03:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This event is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is a C1.8 flare from Active Region 14455 (N15E09) seen peaking at 2026-06-02T02:50Z in SDO AIA 131. A small jet of filament ejecta is visible in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 in association with this flare, and is heavily deflected to the North, likely due to this region sitting just North of a coronal hole.

A small jet of filament ejecta is visible in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 in association with this flare, and is heavily deflected to the North, likely due to this region sitting just North of a coronal hole.

data.note: Bright loop CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-02T12:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME has a faint, diffuse, preceding feature, but not a shock, seen ahead of the main bulk, likely due to the nature of the source eruption. The source of this event is a very gradual filament eruption seen centered at approx. S10E75 as seen in GOES SUVI, STEREO A EUVI and SDO AIA 304. This filament becomes unstable beginning at approx. 2026-06-02T10:30Z and gradually rises off the limb, but does not begin to disconnect from the disk until approx. 2026-06-02T12:00Z. This earlier rise likely accounts for the diffuse feature seen in coronagraphs before the main bulk of the filament ejecta. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in association with this eruption in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

N18 as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-06-02T16:43Z. Wide opening field lines are also visible in association with this eruption in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

data.note: CME first seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-06-02T17:23Z. The CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 as it is likely obscured by the occulting disk. The source of this event is an M3.3 class flare from Active Region 14455 (N13W05) which peaked at 2026-06-02T16:50Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Opening field lines and dimming are also observed in association with this flare in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 211 with the dimming and opening facing Southward, likely indicating some Southern deflection.

data.note: Narrow, faint CME first seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-06-02T18:09Z. This feature is only seen in STEREO A COR2 because it is mostly likely obscured by the occulting disk in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely some additional outflow following CME: 2026-06-02T17:23Z as there is no independent source signature apart from continuous field line fluctuation following CME: 2026-06-02T17:23Z. This CME fades before reached the end of the FOV of STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-02T19:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. There are two source candidates for this CME. The first and most likely is some faint field line movement from beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-06-02T17:30Z following the filament eruption associated with CME: 2026-06-02T17:00Z. The second and less likely candidate is some additional minor ejecta from AR 14455 following CME: 2026-06-02T17:23Z, but measurement indicates that this second source candidate is not a good fit.

A large ejecta is associated with this event which is deflected to the northwest. Additionally, an EUV wave is observed moving northwest of the eruption site, as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.
